fields.summary: TC-669-01: RRO Flag True When Duty Period Release Delay Exceeds Threshold

content.text: Linked Story: CREWCMBR-669
Precondition: A trip exists with a Duty Period (DP) where the actual release datetime exceeds the planned release datetime beyond the RRO threshold. Out of Scope: LCO, LRO, Guarantees, Special Rules.
TEST STEPS
Step
Action
Test Data
Expected Result
Set up a trip with a Duty Period where plannedReleaseDateTimeUTC and actualReleaseDateTimeUTC are populated and the actual exceeds planned beyond the RRO threshold
DP1: plannedRelease = 2026-03-03T22:00:00Z, actualRelease = 2026-03-04T00:05:00Z (125 min delay)
Trip payload is ready with DP release datetimes showing 125 min actual delay beyond planned
Trigger the RRO Lambda to process the Duty Period
DP payload with 125 min release delay
Lambda is invoked successfully without errors
Calculate the difference between actualReleaseDateTimeUTC and plannedReleaseDateTimeUTC for the DP
actual - planned = 125 minutes, RRO threshold = 120 minutes
Difference is calculated as 125 minutes which exceeds the RRO threshold
Verify the rroEligible flag in the lambda output for the Duty Period
RRO threshold exceeded: actual delay = 125 min > 120 min
rroEligible = true
Confirm the DB update lambda persists rroEligible = true for the DP in DynamoDB
Lambda output payload with rroEligible=true
DynamoDB record shows rroEligible = true on the applicable Duty Period
